distinguishing_features: Passive flange-integrated tuned mass damper with discrete masses and springs
Retuning or decoupling a nozzle bending mode from pressure/flow-induced dynamic excitation
No change to nozzle material grade, pressure rating, or operating envelope
Reduction of dynamically amplified root stress rather than detection or inference of thermal damage
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce dynamically amplified cyclic stresses at a pressure-vessel nozzle-to-shell junction without reducing static load capacity or changing the nozzle material.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism addresses resonance-driven vibration, whereas nozzle thermal fatigue is generally dominated by quasi-static constrained thermal stresses, and the candidate neither establishes that thermal cycling excites a dominant nozzle bending mode nor provides a valid basis for the predicted 35% reduction.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a passive flange-mounted TMD to suppress a hypothesized nozzle resonance is not taught or suggested by the cited monitoring and operating-envelope-control prior art.
